name: Thoracic Spine Pain
summary: Pain in the thoracic region that may be mechanical but warrants careful screening because cardiopulmonary, visceral, fracture and systemic causes can mimic musculoskeletal pain.

looksLike: Pain with trunk rotation or prolonged sitting
redFlags: Chest pressure, breathlessness, sweating or exertional symptoms
Fever, cancer history, unexplained weight loss
Significant trauma or osteoporosis/steroid-related fracture risk
New neurological signs or gait disturbance
firstSteps: Screen urgent causes before musculoskeletal treatment
Maintain comfortable walking and thoracic movement when safe
Modify aggravating load temporarily without prolonged rest

assess: Pain with rib excursion in some cases

tests.name: Thoracic Rotation Range of Motion
tests.purpose: Assess movement-related symptom response after serious causes have been screened.
tests.positive: Reproduction of familiar local symptoms or notable asymmetry/restriction.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Screen urgent causes before musculoskeletal treatment
Maintain comfortable walking and thoracic movement when safe
Modify aggravating load temporarily without prolonged rest
dose: Gentle thoracic rotation: 5–8 reps each side, 1–3 times/day if safe
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
do: Progress thoracic mobility, scapular strength and trunk endurance
Restore breathing and rib-cage excursion if restricted
Build tolerance for sitting, lifting and rotation
dose: Rows and trunk endurance: 2–3 sets of 8–15, 2–3 days/week
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Graded return to occupational and sport tasks
dose: Loaded carries/rotation: 2–4 sets, gradual load progression
Task exposure based on symptom response
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: Serious causes excluded or medically managed
Normal or adequate breathing and activity tolerance
Work and lifting tasks progressively restored

structures: Thoracic vertebrae, ribs, costovertebral joints, discs and surrounding muscles may contribute.
mechanism: May be referred from cardiopulmonary or visceral structures
classification: Referred or systemic pain requiring medical assessment
investigations: Medical assessment first when cardiopulmonary, systemic or fracture features are present.
Imaging is guided by trauma, fracture risk, neurological signs and persistent unexplained symptoms.
manual: Thoracic/rib mobilization may be considered only after appropriate medical screening.
Avoid thrust techniques where fracture, osteoporosis risk, malignancy or cardiopulmonary cause is suspected.
modalities: Do not mask unexplained chest or thoracic symptoms with passive modalities.
mistakes: Assuming all thoracic pain is postural
pearls: Thoracic pain deserves a broader differential than routine mechanical low back pain.
Chest symptoms or exertional breathlessness require urgent medical triage.

tests.name: Thoracic Rotation Range of Motion
tests.purpose: Assess movement-related symptom response after serious causes have been screened.
tests.positive: Reproduction of familiar local symptoms or notable asymmetry/restriction.
tests.patientPosition: Seated with pelvis stabilised and arms crossed; clinician observes trunk rotation both directions.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: A mechanical response does not exclude visceral disease; interpret with systemic screening.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
